description: Legal and regulatory obligations and contractual commitments for cybersecurity are identified and managed.
notes: Regulatory scope drives what applies. Banks and non-bank lenders fall under different GLBA rules.

description: Stakeholders set and agree on cybersecurity risk management objectives.
Risk appetite and tolerance statements are set and kept current.
notes: SOC 2 and the Safeguards Rule do not require a formal appetite statement. Mapping is partial.

description: Senior leadership is accountable for cybersecurity risk and promotes a risk aware culture.
notes: Annual board reporting under 314.4(i) is a concrete GLBA example.

description: Cybersecurity roles responsibilities and authorities are established and communicated.
notes: The Safeguards Rule calls this role the Qualified Individual.

description: Resources are allocated in line with the risk strategy and assigned roles.
HR practices include cybersecurity considerations such as screening and offboarding.
Policy based on the risk strategy is established communicated and enforced.
notes: GLBA requires a written information security program.

description: Policy is reviewed and revised as risks and requirements change.
Cybersecurity risk management performance is measured and reviewed for adjustments.
A supply chain risk management program and strategy are established and agreed.
Security requirements are written into contracts and agreements with suppliers.
Risks from suppliers are understood recorded and monitored over the relationship.
Inventories of hardware managed by the organization are maintained.
notes: Asset inventory underpins almost every other control.

description: Inventories of software services and systems are maintained.
Representations of network communication and data flows are maintained.
notes: Loose mapping. None of these frameworks explicitly requires data flow diagrams.

description: Assets are ranked by classification criticality and business impact.
Inventories of data are kept and data types are classified.
Vulnerabilities in assets are identified validated and recorded.
notes: GLBA sets the cadence: annual penetration testing and vulnerability assessments every six months.

description: Internal and external threats are identified and recorded.
Threats vulnerabilities likelihood and impact are used to determine and prioritize risk.
notes: GLBA requires a written risk assessment that is repeated periodically.

description: Risk responses are selected prioritized planned and tracked.
Changes and exceptions are managed assessed for risk and tracked.
Improvements are identified from evaluations such as audits and assessments.

theme: Incident response and cyber plans maintained
description: Cybersecurity plans including incident response and continuity are established communicated and maintained.
Identities and credentials for users services and hardware are issued managed and revoked.
Identities are proofed and bound to credentials based on the context of interactions.
Users services and hardware are authenticated and stronger methods are used for higher risk.
notes: GLBA requires MFA for anyone accessing any information system unless the Qualified Individual approves an equivalent control in writing.

description: Access permissions are defined managed and reviewed using least privilege and separation of duties.
Physical access to assets is managed monitored and enforced.
notes: The Safeguards Rule only touches facilities through asset management. Bank guidelines are more direct.

description: Personnel receive awareness training so they can perform tasks with cybersecurity risk in mind.
Individuals in specialized roles receive training suited to their responsibilities.
The confidentiality integrity and availability of data at rest are protected.
notes: GLBA allows alternative controls approved by the Qualified Individual if encryption is infeasible.

description: The confidentiality integrity and availability of data in transit are protected.
Backups of data are created protected maintained and tested.
notes: GLBA does not explicitly name backups.

description: Configuration management practices are established and applied.
Software is maintained replaced and removed commensurate with risk.
notes: Partial mapping for GLBA. The rule requires vulnerability assessments rather than patching by name.

description: Log records are generated and made available for continuous monitoring.
Installation and execution of unauthorized software are prevented.
Secure software development practices are integrated and their performance is monitored.
Networks and environments are protected from unauthorized logical access and usage.
notes: GLBA is silent on network segmentation by name.

description: Mechanisms are implemented to meet resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations.
Adequate resource capacity is maintained to ensure availability.
Networks and network services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Personnel activity and technology usage are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
External service provider activities and services are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Computing hardware software and runtime environments are monitored to find potentially adverse events.
Potentially adverse events are analyzed to better understand associated activities.
Incidents are declared when adverse events meet defined criteria.
The incident response plan is executed once an incident is declared.
Incident reports are triaged and validated.
Analysis is performed to establish what took place during an incident and its root cause.
Internal and external stakeholders are notified of incidents.
notes: GLBA requires FTC notice within 30 days for events involving 500 or more consumers. Banks have separate agency notification rules with a much shorter window.

description: Incidents are contained.
The recovery portion of the incident response plan is executed once initiated.
The integrity of backups and restoration assets is verified before restoring.
Recovery activities and progress are communicated to designated stakeholders.
